title: Valet Key

validation.research: Four primary sources verified. Microsoft Azure Architecture Center establishes Valet Key as restricted direct-resource delegation with the application authorizing issuance and leaving the transfer path. Azure Storage documents SAS scope/lifetime and different ad hoc/service-policy forms. S3 documents key/method/expiry restrictions, reuse, credential expiry, request-time expiry with ongoing download continuation and later retry failure, plus replacement by presigned uploads. Google Cloud Storage explicitly documents possession-based signed-URL access. No existing exact canonical article found. Signed URLs/SAS are concrete implementations, not universal aliases; no unsupported alias added. Security and Access Boundaries is the primary home because narrowly delegated access is the central mechanism, with performance as a consequence.

sources.supports: Established scoped direct-resource delegation pattern, separate grant issuance/data transfer, permission/resource/time constraints, secure delivery, upload validation and suitability limits.

sources.title: Shared access signatures overview
sources.author: Azure Storage documentation
sources.supports: Resource/permission/lifetime delegation, distinct SAS forms, ad hoc grants and stored access policies supported for service SAS but not user-delegation/account SAS. Revocation capability depends on grant type.

sources.title: Download and upload objects with presigned URLs
sources.author: Amazon S3 documentation
sources.supports: Exact bucket/key/method/expiry inputs, reuse, signer permission and credential lifetime, request-time expiry with existing download continuation/retry failure, and overwrite of existing keys by presigned uploads.

sources.title: Signed URLs
sources.author: Google Cloud Storage documentation
sources.supports: Anyone possessing an active signed URL can use it, required signing authority, limited resource/actions/time, and direct transfer without client storage credentials. Article uses bearer semantics without claiming a universal provider wire format.

example_limits: Sequential in-memory opaque-ticket ledger model, not cloud signing, a provider SDK, live storage integration, TLS/authentication/process isolation, a durable grant service, streaming or concurrent authorization. Trusted Broker ownership and authenticated-subject placeholders control issuance; Storage.grant_download is a privileged administrative fixture operation, not a public endpoint. Storage uses its own trusted virtual clock to enforce GET/exact-key/start<=time<end before body retrieval. Reuse is permitted. Expired ledger rows are not cleaned up. Negative lifecycle witnesses show that changed issuer ownership does not revoke an old ticket and key-bound access can return later replacement bytes. Provider credential expiry/revocation, signed-header constraints, immutable versions, upload validation/publication and direct-transfer auditing remain real deployment responsibilities. Expiry does not recall already returned information or claim to interrupt a live stream.
